news.title: USWNT's 2-2 draw with Spain maps the work that's ahead of the 2027 World Cup for hungry USA soccer
news.desc: The Americans proved that they can compete with the best team in the world, but there is work to do
text: CHESTER, Pa. - From the moment the first ball was kicked, it felt like a game with high stakes between the United States and Spain as titans of the game clashed. In total, 18,648 fans in Chester cheered every clearance, tackle, and promising attack at the top of their lungs until, and as she does to many a team around the world, Alexia Putellas took the air out of the stadium by splitting the USWNT central defense, but they were able to show resilience as Mallory Swanson drew level in the 86th minute of play for a 2-2 draw.

As the road to the 2027 World Cup becomes clearer by the day, one thing is evident. Spain are the team to beat, as no matter who Sonia Bermudez puts in the lineup, Spain will be compact in defense and pull you out of position to finish their own chances. This is a spot the USWNT used to be in, but as Hayes figures out her best XI on the fly while missing key players like Naomi Girma, who was supposed to be in this camp before picking up an injury with Chelsea, there's a way to go in order to defeat the number one team in the world. And that's a fact that Hayes is aware of.
"They're the best team in the world. I didn't learn anything that I didn't already know," Hayes said when asked what she learned during this camp.

While it's not to state that the gap is larger than it is between these teams, it drives home the point that the USWNT now play in a world where they aren't the favorites; they are among the favorites, but it's the little moments that determine how those top sides in the world shake out.

While it seemed like Emily Fox was setting a physical tone early in the match, that bite didn't last, and ball watching helped gift the second goal of the game. On the bright side, part of the path to how the USWNT can get ready for these moments also showcased itself in the same match via Ashley Sanchez. Taking on two Spanish defenders, the N.C. Courage winger was able to secure a great finish in the second half, notching her first start since October of 2024 with a memorable moment.
Ashley's first goal since 2022 🦅USWNT x @vw pic.twitter.com/xRuNztkgE5

You'd want Sanchez's goal to come at a time when the USWNT are level with Spain versus already trailing, but that's the gap that Hayes is looking to close. On their day, this team can defeat anyone in the world; the Olympics have proven that, but now they have to add consistency, which has been lacking during this camp. Being able to fight back is an important quality, and getting Swanson back to her best will be critical for the team to get where they want to be. In only six matches in Paris, Swanson scored four goals and assisted two more, and while the attack is deep, she's a game changer.

It's great to see someone confident in their finishes, and Sanchez was just that, cutting in from the left wing. Most days she'll generate more than .17 xG, but also, if that's all that she needs to score, the USWNT will benefit from it.
These were also meaningful goals for their teammates to see too.

"I'm so pumped for them. Sanchez is back for the first time in a bit, and I think she earned that goal. She's been playing so incredibly for her club, and I think she capitalized on the opportunities that she was given, and she did great," Rose Lavelle said. "I think for Mal, coming back from having a baby is no easy feat at all, and she does it with such grace, and I'm just happy for them both. And for the team to have two players who can come into a game like this and do that is incredible for us."

Teams like Spain exposing flaws is a good thing since it gives Hayes and the squad things to fine-tune when they get together again in November for the Concacaf W Championship facing El Salvador, when they won't have a long layoff between camps like they did between facing Brazil in June and now in October. That makes it easier for Hayes to continue building relationships because the structure is there as they enter the competition that serves as World Cup qualifying.

Alyssa Thompson echoed how important it is to play in these games, not only so that they can be challenges for the players who have been to major tournaments, but for those trying to make their first, it's a great chance to measure yourself against the best in the world and see where you need to grow.

Only time will improve how passes between the squad find each other, and knowing when to shoot or take on their defenders. There's also the bright spot of Kate Del Fava getting an assist on her USWNT debut, which is yet another thing to build. Hayes has now used 46 players this year with the USWNT, which is a new record as she ensures she sees what she has in each of them. When a new player makes a debut like Del Fava today, the team is also undefeated, which is an excellent sign when looking to find these combinations.

It's all about Hayes putting her Legos in the right configuration because this team can beat Spain, and to win the World Cup, they may need to, and they'll just need to configure the pieces in the right order. And when you want a tactician to lead the ship, there's no one that the USWNT would rather have at the helm than Hayes to set the squad up, building off of these friendlies for what they hope will be a run to the World Cup final.

news.title: Lisandro Martinez just said what every Man United fan is thinking after embarrassing UCL loss at Atletico
news.desc: United lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, and their Argentine defender did not hold back as their horrible start to the season continues
text: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez did not hold back on his team after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid, arguing the Red Devils' squad is not strong enough to compete in Europe's top club competition.

United conceded in the first minute thanks to a goal from Alex Baena, while Ademola Lookman bagged a second in the 79th minute of a dominant performance from the Spanish side. The result leaves United with just three wins in nine games across all competitions this season, which is Michael Carrick's first full campaign as the head coach after taking over the role last winter.

"We're not playing well as a team," Martinez said on the UEFA Champions League Today post-match show. "You can see the disconnection. We can't [string] three or four passes together, and the body language [is bad]. We missed some chances, we are negative, and yeah, when you play against these teams, especially in Champions League, you can't miss opportunities and you can't concede the goal we conceded in the first minutes."
Martinez used the opportunity to push for higher standards, arguing that United are capable of more than their record suggests.

"Trying to be positive and trying to be honest," he added. "We have to change, to do more. Because we are capable to do better. We have the players. But also, when you watch television and watch the games, you see the players and the managers and you put the finger [and blame them], which is right. We take the responsibility, but also as a club, I expect more. I'm not gonna close my mouth. I expect more. We need more ambition. We need to talk more about winning Champions League, talk more about winning the Premier League instead of other things."

Martinez, who joined the Red Devils in the summer of 2022, also reflected on the fact that the team has been in a period of inconsistency for the entirety of his time with the club. United's ups and downs, though, stretch back more than a decade; they last won the Premier League title in the 2012-13 in what was Sir Alex Ferguson's final season in charge, his shadow looming large since.
"Every season, we're talking about the same thing," Martinez said. "Of course, but if we don't say the truth, nothing will change."
Atleti manager Diego Simeone was also critical of United's approach over the course of the game, one that ultimately suited his side just fine despite the surprise.

"We knew what they were going to do," Simeone told the UEFA Champions League Today post-match show. "We needed to find the opposite side from where they started their press ... we knew we could find success there. In the first half, we would press their right flank a lot of the times and Baena or Grimaldo would find that space behind to launch an attack and start an important transition like we had in various opportunities. We knew that if we beat their press, we would find ourselves with tons of space to run, like we did with the first goal"
Martinez repeated his sentiments in different post-match broadcast interviews over the course of the evening, hitting a particularly harsh note in his discussion with Amazon Prime.

"Really poor," he said. "Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment. We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today. I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

news.title: Champions League expert picks, predictions, best bets: Can Man City top PSG in high-pressure return to Etihad?
news.desc: Check out all the picks from our experts as the Champions League league phase rolls on
text: The Champions League is finally back. Five weeks after an opening matchday that delivered goals aplenty, Europe's elite return to the league phase on Tuesday and Wednesday, and the Matchday 2 slate wastes no time getting serious. Wednesday's headliner comes at the Etihad, where Manchester City host Paris Saint-Germain in what is City's first UCL game since they were found guilty of 114 financial charges. Their first game since the charges was actually on Sunday at Liverpool, and that went more than well.

Real Madrid, 2-1 winners over Inter in their opener, head to Rome with their former coach Jose Mourinho already fuming, while many giants are on upset alert with some intriguing away clashes, including Barcelona's visit to Istanbul to take on Galatasaray.
Then there's Como. The Serie A side stunned RB Leipzig 4-1 in their first-ever Champions League match and now visit Feyenoord looking to prove that night was no fluke.

Every match streams live on Paramount+, your home for every Champions League game all season long, plus replays, highlights and studio coverage breaking down the race for the top eight. If you haven't signed up yet, now's the time.

Person to watch: Pep Guardiola, N.A. -- When news of Manchester City having committed 114 breaches of Premier League rules arrived over the international break, many wondered how Pep Guardiola, their manager of a decade before leaving in the summer, might react. After all, he had previously said he would walk out of the club if he found out they had lied to him over their skirting of financial rules. Instead, Guardiola has rallied behind his former club in remarkable fashion, offering public support to the ownership. He is due to go one step further on Wednesday night, showing up at City's first home game since the verdict. Up in the Etihad stands, all eyes will be on Guardiola. Will he be able to avoid the temptation for some tactical tinkering? -- James Benge

Man of the match: Kvicha Kvaratskhelia -- PSG: The Georgian winger only scored one goal so far in the opening six Ligue 1 games and he's expected to react in the coming weeks, as he's been a key player for Luis Henrique and PSG over the past two years since he joined from Napoli. He left his mark in the two Champions League finals won by the French giants in the past two seasons and he's also a serious candidate for the 2026 Ballon d'Or. -- Francesco Porzio

Prediction: Manchester City 2, Paris Saint-Germain 2 -- This match is brought to you by sovereign wealth funds, ones who have a well-documented ability to build superteams that can headline Champions League games, no matter the controversy. Manchester City's win over Liverpool on Sunday proved that the team are doing what they can: somehow focus on the games in front of them despite the possibility of serious penalties for financial breaches of epic proportions, so much so that they will be hard to count out against Paris Saint-Germain. Whether or not the result feels tainted, though, is another question entirely. -- Pardeep Cattry

Best bet: Erling Haaland to have 2+ shots on target (-140) -- There are plenty of reasons off the pitch to keep an eye on City's return to their home stadium but if anyone can rise above and keep producing, it's Haaland. He was able to score to silence the Anfield crowd and while goals will be hard to come by in this game, he'll have his chances to test the keeper for shots on target during this clash. -- Charles Booth

news.title: On night of mayhem for Liverpool, Barcola arrives in style
news.desc: Bradley Barcola's form was the subject of pre-match questions before Liverpool faced LASK - but the France forward's Champions League hat-trick was the perfect answer.
text: On the eve of Liverpool's meeting with LASK, manager Andoni Iraola was repeatedly asked about the fortunes of Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola.

Given their price tags, the pressure was on both to start delivering after stuttering starts to their individual campaigns. Iraola, as most managers would, stood by his players, insisting he trusted them "100%".

Iraola insisted the focus was on the collective rather than individual stats but there is no denying that when you spend such eye-watering sums - £116m on Wirtz and £123m on Barcola - you want those players to be match-winners.
Wirtz delivered a fine display in the Austrian city of Linz as Liverpool won 6-3, with an assist to show for his efforts.
However, this was a night where the headlines belonged to Barcola, who on the 238th appearance of his career across clubs and country combined, scored his first hat-trick.
And it was those three goals which proved to be the difference as Liverpool returned to winning ways after their 3-0 loss to Manchester City on Sunday.

In truth, the 24-year-old could have scored more such was his quality, but he did enough to take the match ball home after two fine finishes with his right foot and left foot, followed by a tap in after the break.
And a little over 24 hours after defending his players against those pre-match questions, Iraola was speaking with a smile on his face.
"You were asking me yesterday about him not making the numbers and [the same with] Florian and I think both of them today played really, really well. I think they made a difference.
"Bradley was a threat, always when one-on-one [and] certainly in behind. He helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am and happy for both of them.
"I think for their confidence it's very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. I think it's going to be very good, very good for them."
On what it could mean for Barcola, Iraola added: "I think he has to enjoy this [as] to score a hat-trick in the Champions League is always very difficult.
"Even yesterday in training, I could feel he was very lively. Sometimes you feel these things [are going to happen]. We were feeling he was in a good place going into the game."
Barcola will now hope to show that level in the Premier League, starting with a visit to Brentford on Saturday.
Iraola's side were relentless in the first-half against the Austrian Bundesliga champions, racing into a three-goal lead. Such was their dominance, they could have easily scored more.
The 19 shots Liverpool had by half time against LASK was the most on record since 2003-04 by any team in the first half of a Champions League away match.
If there was any criticism, it would be that they were guilty of becoming a little complacent in the second half, conceding three goals after the hour mark but in fairness, the job was all but done.

There were more positives to take on the night, with both full-backs coming into the side and performing well. Jeremie Frimpong scored and registered two assists while Kostas Tsimikas added two assists of his own.
Ronald Araujo also scored his first goal for the club since joining in the summer and Lewis Koumas got no less than he deserved when he got on the scoresheet in the second half.

The 21-year-old even had two goals ruled out for offside but his first-half assist for Barcola meant that he became the youngster player to score and assist in a Champions League match for Liverpool (21y 25d), with the previous youngest being Steven Gerrard (21y 139d v Dynamo Kyiv in 2001). Fine company, indeed.
But Liverpool will know that they won’t get many easier games than this over the course of the season. LASK came into this game, winless in their last four matches.
“What do you take from that? It's very difficult because the game was very passive for large periods,” said Stephen Warnock on 5 Live.
”There were parts where I am watching Trey Nyoni in midfield and he has literally got no pressure on him at all, he is picking passes off.
“Barcola has got the run of his full-back who was taken off at half-time, which tells you everything.
“I don't read too much into it, because I expected Liverpool to go there and win, and win comfortably."
Warnock added that a bigger test for Liverpool will come at Brentford on Saturday, the Bees fourth in the table and unbeaten in the league.
“Can Barcola do that again, away at Brentford, because that is what they have essentially bought him for, to play in big games away from home," Warnock said.
“He hasn't played that much football this season so [this game] was about getting minutes in his legs and getting him fit and getting him sharper. The acid test will be Brentford away.”

news.title: Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout
news.desc: Lisandro Martinez's explosive comments after Manchester United's Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid turn the spotlight back on director of football Jason Wilcox.
text: It is almost 10 months since Jason Wilcox was in the line of fire when Ruben Amorim gave the explosive post-match news conference at Leeds that triggered his dismissal.
Amorim was furious Manchester United's director of football had subtly advised him to change tactics for the previous game against Wolves.
"I will do my job and every department, the scouting department, the sporting director, needs to do theirs," said Amorim.
Less than 24 hours after that chiding, Amorim was sacked, and the focus was on the part Wilcox played in that.
This time Lisandro Martinez was doing the firing and had a target in mind.
He might have got the job title slightly wrong, but there was no doubting who Martinez meant after the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid when he said: "I expect more from our technical director."
There is no doubting either that Martinez knew what he was saying.

Working as a post-match interviewer for US broadcaster CBS, legendary former United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel tried to steer Martinez away from discussion about his old club's summer transfer window on four occasions. Each time, the Argentina defender refused to be deflected.
"We don't have the best squad at the moment compared to other top teams," said Martinez.
"I'm not going to close my mouth. We need more ambition. If we don't say the truth, nothing will change."

During the summer, BBC Sport was told by dressing room sources the club needed to sign more players than the three - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba - who eventually arrived, and it was "fairly obvious" where they needed to be - left-back and striker.
Another source with extensive knowledge of the inner workings at Old Trafford describes the current situation as "a mess".
Quiz: Do you remember the big names who took aim at football club chiefs?

Martinez said he felt it was important to speak out the way he did. Many United fans are delighted he went down that path, and the defender was highlighting inadequacies in the club's leadership structure.
The first is that Martinez's contract expires at the end of the season. United have the option to extend it by another year.

By being so outspoken against senior figures at the club, was he trying to ensure that option is not triggered, which would allow him to leave for nothing in the summer, or, potentially, for a lower fee in January?

Martinez is good friends with Atletico Madrid defender Cristian Romero and the international colleagues spoke after last night's game. Romero was similarly forceful against the Tottenham hierarchy last season.
Also, while the vast majority of United fans may agree with Martinez, internally his comments create a problem.

Most obviously, head coach Michael Carrick, having deflected questions about the defender's outburst in the immediate aftermath of the game, will face more probing on the matter when he speaks to the media before Sunday's trip to Leeds.

Any players lined up to talk around the Elland Road trip will be similarly quizzed. When Tielemans was asked about it by Amazon Prime on Tuesday night, he replied with a "no comment". Given the comments about recruitment, he would clearly be within his rights to ask Martinez outright "did you mean me?"
Carrick has to manage the delicate dressing room dynamic at a point when he needs a collective focus on trying to win enough matches to keep him in a job.
Sources who know the United boss well are adamant there is no better person to handle the turmoil, and it is at times of crisis like this that his innate calmness is a major strength.
However, after five games without a win, it is a problem Carrick could do without.
United sources say the 55-year-old is not in any danger of losing his job.

The club's recruitment department is working on potential targets for January given it is accepted the strategy of not signing left-back competition for Luke Shaw and striking support for Benjamin Sesko was flawed.

Both players have missed matches already this term, with Sesko sidelined for an indefinite period after suffering a recurrence of the shin issue that flared up in May and prevented him from playing any part in United's pre-season matches.
Unlike other major footballing countries on the continent, there is no expectation for sporting or technical directors to speak to the media.
Former United sporting director Dan Ashworth did it once during his five months at the club and was sitting alongside chief executive Omar Berrada.
Wilcox's only extensive interview since he was appointed in April 2024 has been with United's in-house media, when a couple of answers stood out.
"I am a coach at heart," said the former Blackburn Rovers and Leeds United winger, who spent several years working in coaching at Manchester City's academy.

"I am a coach inside, even though I know I have a different job now. That is a strength in my role, but it also causes me a bit of a problem because I always want to interfere in what the managers are doing."
Regarding his strategy for dealing with stress, Wilcox said: "My wife will know when I am bogged down with frustration. When I re-energise, I do it on my own. Me and the dog, walking."

Wilcox has only spoken briefly to the media after matches on a couple of occasions: after the 2-1 win at Crystal Palace last November, when he told journalists to "trust the process"; then again in Gothenburg after the pre-season encounter with Paris St-Germain when he enthused about the potential pairing of Tielemans and skipper Bruno Fernandes.

Recruitment was praised in summer 2025, when Senne Lammens was signed ahead of Emi Martinez, who was Amorim's preference, and Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo, plus Sesko, reinvigorated United's attack.

But the jury is out on the players acquired in the £155m summer outlay this year: Baleba, who missed the first six weeks of the season with injury; Santos, who has been an unused substitute in the last three Premier League games; and Tielemans, whose form has been patchy.

Sources have questioned the overall strategy, and specifically why Tielemans, who has a similar profile to England international Kobbie Mainoo, was signed, even for £35m, and if the £50m committed to Santos would have been better spent on someone who would be a first choice.
Trust is eroding among United fans over the minority ownership, agreed on Christmas Eve in 2023.
They might look at the other clubs where Ineos have an influence.
Nice are ninth in the French league and Lausanne-Sport are bottom in Switzerland. This doesn't generate a sense of a wider footballing vision that is paying dividends.

At Old Trafford, questions are being asked for the third season in a row over managers who were backed by the hierarchy in the summer. Erik ten Hag was sacked after nine Premier League games in 2024. Amorim went after 20 matches last season.

news.title: Fifa to offer extra £2.6bn for football development
news.desc: Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development across the world.
text: Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn (£2.6bn) increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development across the world.
World football's governing body wants to release the money from its reserves in a move which would more than double the level of planned distribution funding for 2027-2030.
It says it has been able to release the extra cash because of the commercial success of this summer's World Cup.

The proposal will be made at a meeting of Fifa's council on Thursday and comes at a time when the organisation is under pressure following president Gianni Infantino's aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan.

Infantino wanted to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors but faced huge criticism for the proposal, with Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation questioning his position.
Uefa and Concacaf wrote to Infantino in September calling on Fifa to pay at least $10m (£7.5m) from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.

In a letter then sent to Fifa's six continental confederations, Infantino - who will be standing for re-election for a fourth time in March 2027 - said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".

Fifa will now offer extra money from its reserves in addition to the current $2.7bn (£2.05bn) budgeted to be paid to all 211 member associations, the confederations, regional associations and certain non-Fifa affiliated associations.
In total, Fifa will now be spending $6.35bn (£4.83bn) on football development for the 2027-2030 cycle, with a focus on investment and development of women's and youth football.
• $8.25m (£6.3m) for each of the 13 zonal/regional associations
• $1.1m (£836,000) for 100 member associations for travel and equipment solidarity
• One third would be allocated to women's and youth football development
• One third would be allocated to infrastructure (of which there shall be equal access to women's and youth football)
The plan, including the eligibility, application, approval, disbursement, control and audit requirements, will be finalised by the Fifa council at its next meeting in December 2026.
It will all be subject to approval by the 77th Fifa congress in March 2027.

BBC Sport understands there is a proposal on the table at the council to change the disciplinary code and prevent a repeat of the Folarin Balogun situation, an unprecedented scenario which meant the US striker did not miss a game after being sent off in the World Cup.
If approved, it will be expressly noted in the regulations that an automatic one-match ban for a red card cannot be suspended.
Questions have been raised over the process which led to Balogun having his ban suspended.
US President Donald Trump said he called Infantino to get the ban rescinded, which raised serious concerns over political interference.
A proposal has been put forward to add to Article 27 of the regulations a list of instances whereby a ban cannot be suspended.
Infantino broke trust 'through deception' - confederation presidents

news.title: Cokayne back as England face Canada threat in Toronto
news.desc: England welcome back the experience of Amy Cokayne at hooker as their 41-match unbeaten run comes under serious threat away to Canada.
text: England welcome back the experienced Amy Cokayne at hooker as their 41-match unbeaten run goes on the line against Rugby World Cup runners-up Canada in Toronto on Friday.
Cokayne has not played Test rugby since scoring the Red Roses' final try in a Grand Slam-sealing win over France in Bordeaux in May.
Saracens' Bryony Field, who has three caps to Cokayne's 94, drops to the bench after deputising impressively in the first half of the WXV Global Series last month.
During that part of the campaign, Canada ended England's near four-year winning streak with a nail-biting 26-26 draw at Sandy Park in Exeter.
Coach Kevin Rouet has targeted victory over the Red Roses as the main aim for Canada in 2026, with his team playing on home soil for the first time in more than 14 months.
Canada also play England in Ottawa on Friday, 23 October, with the two matches branded as the hosts' Rugby Rematch Tour.

The attendance for the Toronto match is expected to exceed 14,000, comfortably beating the previous record for a standalone women's rugby match in North America which was set when 11,453 watched Canada beat the United States in the most recent home match.
Elsewhere in England's line-up, prop Hannah Botterman features after coming on as a replacement in the dramatic win over New Zealand last time out.

With Marlie Packer staying in England as her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan is due to give birth, Abi Burton takes a spot in the back row, while Tatyana Heard's direct running is preferred to Helena Rowland's playmaking ability at inside centre.
Sadia Kabeya, who missed the win over the Black Ferns with a leg injury, is on the bench, alongside Bristol Bears' 20-year-old Demelza Short, who covers second row.
"The first Test in Exeter gave us a valuable opportunity to test our game under pressure and identify where we can improve," England head coach John Mitchell said.
"Playing in Toronto presents a different environment and challenge, and we're excited by the opportunity to express our game, improve our performance and continue to grow as the Red Roses."
England's last loss came in the Rugby World Cup final against New Zealand in November 2022.
England: Kildunne; Breach, Jones, Heard, Moloney-MacDonald; Harrison, L Packer; Botterman, Cokayne, Bern, Talling, Ives Campion, Burton, Matthews, Feaunati.
Replacements: Field, Carson, Muir, Short, Kabeya, Hunt, Rowland, Sing.

news.title: Man City v PSG LIVE: Wild six-goal thriller in Champions League enthralls returning Pep Guardiola
news.desc: Manchester City 2-4 Paris Saint-Germain: PSG were made to hang on after their first-half masterclass as Erling Haaland scored twice and had many chances to complete his hat-trick
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
Manchester City 2-4 Paris Saint-Germain: PSG were made to hang on after their first-half masterclass as Erling Haaland scored twice and had many chances to complete his hat-trick
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Paris Saint-Germain produced a statement first-half display before Manchester City threatened a remarkable comeback in a thrilling second-half performance as the Champions League holders ran out 4-2 winners at the Etihad.

City were initially blown away in front of the returning former City boss Pep Guardiola as Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha struck for the visitors and Achraf Hakimi hit the post in a rampant 17-minute spell, with PSG becoming the first team to score three first-half goals against City away from home since Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in November 2015.

Enzo Maresca made a triple change at the break and it sparked an improved showing from City, who pulled one back when Erling Haaland headed in and had several chances to score another. City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was then unable to keep out a shot from Maghnes Akliouche as PSG scored a fourth, but Haaland pulled another back for City shortly after he had hit the bar.

Haaland was denied a hat-trick as PSG goalkeeper Matveii Safonov produced a point-blank save and there was still time for former City forward Ferran Torres to roll a tame penalty straight at Donnarumma after Spain’s World Cup winner had been handed the chance to make it five for the European champions.

City were playing their first match at home since they were found guilty of almost all of the club’s breaches of the Premier League financial rules. With City appealing the decision and continuing to maintain their innocence, Maresca’s side were supported by former manager Guardiola, who returned to the Etihad for the first time since his departure in May and looked typically on edge in the stands as he enjoyed a six-goal thriller.
Penny for Pep’s thoughts? He was animated as ever from the stands and often deep in discussion with the City higher-ups.
Elsewhere on a very busy night of Champions League action, here’s how it all finished...

City had 27 shots, PSG 15, with nine and 10 on target respectively. Plus 52 and 17 touches in the opposition box respectively. Big night for all-out attacking football. The less said about the defending, the better...
In the midst of all that, Haaland became City’s all-time record goalscorer in the Champions League.
Luis Enrique and Enzo Maresca share a warm hug. Donnarumma has a nice chat with his former teammates, no bad blood there.
‘90: O’Reilly, who has been preparing to come on for the last eight minutes or so, comes on for Fernandez.
‘89: Nunes does bring him down, sliding in, but he can’t believe it, and you’ve certainly seen more concrete penalties not given. But it stands.
Ex-City man Ferran Torres is resoundingly booed as he steps up to take it... it’s a poor attempt and Donnarumma saves it!!

news.title: Man City and PSG respond to uncertain future by playing out Champions League classic
news.desc: Manchester City 2-4 Paris Saint-Germain: Two breathless halves of football, one a masterclass from PSG and the other a rousing comeback from the hosts, may prove to be the final Champions League classic at the Etihad for some time
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Manchester City 2-4 Paris Saint-Germain: Two breathless halves of football, one a masterclass from PSG and the other a rousing comeback from the hosts, may prove to be the final Champions League classic at the Etihad for some time
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
It was far from the first Champions League classic Pep Guardiola has seen at the Etihad Stadium even if Manchester City’s plight means it may prove the last.

If Guardiola’s first return to the club he managed for an increasingly controversial decade had seemed designed to provide a show of support in the wake of 114 guilty verdicts, the drama that followed suggested that it was simply a footballing choice. Guardiola witnessed something extraordinary.

There was a time when his City were Europe’s outstanding team. Now that mantle has passed to Luis Enrique’s Paris Saint-Germain. Yet even as they delivered a masterclass, City responded with a show of spirit. It may be dangerous to draw too many parallels to events off the field, where they require a still more remarkable comeback. If nothing else, Enzo Maresca’s players illustrated that they have not abandoned hope. Guardiola’s former assistant again showed he can change games with his substitutions.

Nevertheless, the footballing statement came from the defending champions. Theirs was an exhibition of eminence. Their first-half display may have been the best performance here in the Champions League since Guardiola’s City beat Real Madrid 4-0 in the 2023 semi-final. The broader conclusion may be that it illustrated how times have changed since then.

If City’s only route back into the Champions League is by winning it – which, given possible Premier League sanctions, could be the case – this was a reminder that PSG are the team to beat. Even as Erling Haaland led the assault on the PSG goal in the second half, City were beaten for the fourth time in eight home Champions League games.

PSG had killed them with kindness in becoming outspoken anomalies, defending City in the wake of the independent commission’s verdict. They then eviscerated them with excellence. If it was a hugely entertaining distraction from City’s off-field issues, perhaps it was telling it came at the hands of a club who have had their own brushes with Financial Fair Play before constructing this wonderful team, though it was testament to the talents of Luis Enrique and his team as well as their considerable resources.

It said something that the outstanding player in last season’s Champions League, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, was held in reserve. They could afford to confine him to a cameo. Desire Doue starred on the left wing in his absence. He was pivotal in PSG’s devastating double, two goals in as many minutes to set them on their way. Thereafter, the action was non-stop.

It was typical of a topsy-turvy night that it ended with a penalty save from Gianluigi Donnarumma to deny Ferran Torres, with each facing his former club. PSG would not have won their maiden Champions League in 2025 without some extraordinary saves from Donnarumma in the knockout stages. But, in his first reunion with them, the Italian was arguably culpable for the opener and beaten in freakish fashion for the visitors’ fourth goal when he made a flying save from Maghnes Akliouche, only for the ball to spin in. The winger, too, showed the reigning champions have alternatives to Kvaratskhelia.

When PSG had pulled clear, Doue’s 20-yard drive defeated Donnarumma at the near post. Some 99 seconds later, they scored again courtesy of a wonderful long-range one-two from Ousmane Dembele and Doue, the elder Frenchman playing a cross-field ball to the younger and meeting his lobbed cross with a far-post header. Dembele had escaped from Marc Guehi. It was far from the only time he proved elusive; Guardiola, who had such success with a false nine at Barcelona, saw a former teammate, in Luis Enrique, borrow that tactic to great effect.

The roving right-back Achraf Hakimi felt similarly hard to track and, after he headed Doue’s cross against the post, Vitinha curled in a shot when Warren Zaire-Emery, with a backheeled flick, touched on Akliouche’s cutback.

At that stage, a rout beckoned. Yet Maresca’s managerial career had peaked with a tactical masterclass when his Chelsea beat PSG 3-0 in the Club World Cup final. When 3-0 down, he exerted a remarkable impact.
A half-time triple change worked, with Ayyoub Bouaddi bolstering the midfield and City suddenly creating so many chances they finished with 27 shots.

The substitute Iliman Ndiaye had an effort repelled by Matvei Safonov. He crossed when Haaland headed in, to get Guardiola clapping. It brought a reminder that PSG can look frail when put under pressure, even if Akliouche temporarily relieved it.

Yet City kept on coming. Nuno Mendes cleared Josko Gvardiol’s header off the line. City twice struck the woodwork Enzo Fernandez hitting the outside of the post and Haaland heading against the bar. The Norwegian doubled his tally from Bouaddi’s pass.

Safonov, who sometimes looks an unworthy successor to Donnarumma, made a wonderful save to deny Haaland a hat-trick and perhaps finally finish off City. Torres had the chance to do so definitively but Donnarumma stopped the Spaniard from adding a fifth to PSG. And so, amid all the action, this became a successor to spectacular Champions League nights here.

news.title: Aston Villa run riot in record-breaking win over Fenerbahce as Mason Greenwood taunted on UK return
news.desc: Aston Villa hit Fenerbahce for six on a memorable night at Villa Park
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
Aston Villa hit Fenerbahce for six on a memorable night at Villa Park
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Mason Greenwood suffered a miserable return to English football as his Fenerbahce team were swept aside 6-0 by a rampant Aston Villa side in the Champions League.

The 25-year-old was playing his first match in this country since his suspension by Manchester United in January 2022, facing taunts from home fans who thoroughly enjoyed an electric Villa Park display.
Johan Manzambi marked his 21st birthday with a goal before Nicolas Jackson scored a double to give Villa a 3-0 lead at half-time.
A second-half brace from Ross Barkley and a late finish by Tammy Abraham completed the rout over the Turkish side, delighting the Prince of Wales, who gave his royal seal of approval from the stands.

It was Villa’s largest ever European victory and provided their first home win of the season. The result leaves them strongly positioned in the early Champions League standings with two victories from two, ahead of an inviting home game against Viking next week.
Villa supporters ensured Greenwood was given a hostile reception on his return to playing in England after four-and-a-half years.
The winger’s last appearance for United came in January 2022, eight days before he was charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm.
He denied the charges, and the CPS discontinued the case in February 2023.
The Villa crowd targeted him with persistent boos and derogatory chants during the opening period.
The home support soon turned their attention to celebrating as Villa’s energetic start yielded a 12th-minute opener.
John McGinn’s corner landed for birthday boy Manzambi, whose shot took a deflection off Milan Skriniar and went in.
Fenerbahce offered a bright response with chances to equalise, but Vedat Muriqi was twice thwarted by Zion Suzuki, who also dealt with a weak strike by Greenwood.
Villa doubled their advantage in the 31st minute when Jackson got off the mark.
Boubacar Kamara dispossessed the opposition high up the pitch and found the former Chelsea striker, who drilled a low shot into the bottom corner from 18 yards.
The Turkish side remained a constant threat and ought to have scored soon after, but Oguz Aydin crashed his shot against the crossbar after breaking behind the Villa defence.
Instead, Villa were left celebrating once more as they made it 3-0 in the 39th minute.
McGinn reclaimed possession and Barkley set up Jackson, who placed his finish into a similar spot to his first goal.
Villa had to wait until the 68th minute to score a fourth, though Jackson – who was on a hat-trick – did not take the penalty after Manzambi was fouled by Ismail Yuksek.
Instead, Barkley converted from the spot and four minutes later he scored again as a deflected strike from the edge of the area wrong-footed former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson.
Abraham completed an emphatic victory in the 90th minute, turning the ball in from close range after fine work by winger Alysson.

news.title: How Bradley Barcola scored his Liverpool hat-trick, but were defensive lapses a concern?
news.desc: LASK 3-6 Liverpool: Andoni Iraola’s side enjoyed a big Champions League win as Lewis Koumas also got on the scoresheet in Austria
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
LASK 3-6 Liverpool: Andoni Iraola’s side enjoyed a big Champions League win as Lewis Koumas also got on the scoresheet in Austria
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Bradley Barcola got off the mark for Liverpool in style with a Champions League hat-trick in a 6-3 win against LASK in Austria.
The France international winger did not score in his first five appearances for the Reds after arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in deal that could rise to £123m.
But the 24-year-old bagged his first senior hat-trick of his career as Liverpool ran riot against the Austrian champions.
Defender Ronald Araujo also scored his first Liverpool goal with the first of the night, while Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas were also on target for Andoni Iraola’s side.
Welsh forward Koumas, who started in place of the injured Alexander Isak, scored his first Liverpool goal in two-and-a-half years after the 21-year-old had two goals ruled out earlier.
While Liverpool’s forward line threatened all night, there was sloppiness at the back in the closing stages and Iraola will be disappointed to have conceded three for the second game in a row.
But a second consecutive win in the Champions League, following the opening victory over Atletico Madrid, got Iraola’s side back on track following Sunday’s 3-0 defeat to Manchester City.
Ironically, the standout winger on the night was arguably Rio Ngumoha, with the 18-year-old tormenting LASK throughout with his direct dribbling and trickery out wide.
But it was Barcola who produced the clinical touches in the area, adding to his electric bursts of speed and movement behind the LASK backline.
Ngumoha was the spark for Barcola’s first Liverpool goal, working his way into the box before a clever flick from Koumas allowed Barcola to sweep a first-time finish into the far corner.
Barcola’s second was created by Florian Wirtz, who responded to the criticism of his performance against City with a piercing through ball between LASK defenders and into Barcola’s feet.
After his earlier strike, two quick touches from the former PSG winger displayed his confidence and eye for goal, with a low left-footed finish slotted into the bottom corner.
Barcola’s third to complete the hat-trick was the simplest of the three, owing to being in the right place at the right time after Ngumoha had slipped in Frimpong to square across goal.
“I think he played so well today and not just the goals,” Iraola said of Barcola’s performance. “He had more chances to score and he was always a threat attacking the spaces in behind.
“In training sometimes you feel when a player is in the zone, and fortunately tonight for us he has shown the level that he has.”
Koumas was rewarded for another committed performance leading the line and the academy product showed how much a Champions League goal meant for the Reds with his celebration.
“He has to enjoy it because he deserves it,” Iraola said. “I think he scored two disallowed goals which is unlucky for him but he kept pressing, making the runs in behind and doing his job.
“I think it’s fair that he score his goal and can have his moment of celebration with the supporters.”
In all, it added up to a pleasing attacking performance for Iraola, with Ngumoha and Koumas again impressing in the absence of Isak and Cody Gakpo and Barcola and Wirtz making impacts too.
“I’m very happy with the performance,” Iraola added. “Today I think we were very aggressive with the ball. Sometimes you talk aggressiveness without the ball but I’m talking about with the ball.
“I think we took good positions, we moved the ball well, attacked the spaces well.”
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk was given a rare evening off, with left-back Kostas Tsimikas wearing the armband in his absence and Araujo and Jeremy Jacquet starting at centre-back.
Jacquet continued his excellent start to life at Liverpool with another impressing while Araujo’s first goal, rising from a corner to head in the delivery from Tsimikas, was a bonus as well.
Where it went wrong defensively for Liverpool, having largely dominated LASK from the outset, was when Iraola made changes to the backline while the Reds were leading 4-0.
It is unusual to see a centre-back pair swapped mid-game but Van Dijk and Joe Gomez were brought on for Jacquet and Araujo in a double-change on the hour.
Liverpool were immediately caught cold as Robert Ljubicic pulled one back. Then, after Barcola and Koumas had stretched Liverpool’s lead to 6-1, Florian Flecker struck twice for the hosts.
Both goals looked preventable, sure, and Alisson conceded three times from four shots on target.
But given the game had been won and Liverpool were already looking towards Saturday’s trip to Brentford in the Premier League, they won’t be too much of a concern.
“It’s probably the reason why the manager shouldn’t change both centre-backs!” Iraola said.
“But we were already winning 4-0 and you have to think about the next game and saving the legs of the players. We didn’t defend properly at the end of the game."

news.title: ‘An exhibition’: Steven Gerrard salutes PSG after stunning first half against Man City
news.desc: Doue, Dembele and Vitinha struck for the back-to-back Champions League winners, in the first time City had conceded three first-half goals at home since 2015
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
Doue, Dembele and Vitinha struck for the back-to-back Champions League winners, in the first time City had conceded three first-half goals at home since 2015
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Steven Gerrard hailed “a 31-minute exhibition” from Paris Saint-Germain as the best football he had seen in years after the Champions League holders scored three first-half goals against Manchester City.
Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha struck for the visitors and Achraf Hakimi hit the post in a rampant 17-minute spell while former City manager Pep Guardiola watched on at the Etihad.

Guardiola was making his first appearance at the Etihad since leaving the club in May, in what was City’s first home appearance since the were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

But PSG became the first team to score three first-half goals against Manchester City away from home since Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in November 2015 as Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions produced a statement performance.

And former Liverpool captain Gerrard was stunned to see a City side who have won all six of their Premier League games this season and were 3-0 winners at Anfield on Sunday be so comprehensively outplayed.

“It’s been a 31-minute exhibition, it’s been so one-sided,” Gerrard said on TNT Sports. “Outstanding. I think Enzo Maresca has to speak to his staff and change something. I think they’re a man down in the centre of the pitch with [Rayan] Cherki.”

Former England international Owen Hargreaves called PSG’s football “ridiculous” and said: “The quality of the touches and finishing [from PSG] is exquisite. That is as good as I’ve seen live maybe ever. Technically this is best of what the Premier League has to offer and they’ve put on a masterclass.”

news.title: Arsenal cutting jobs just days after Mikel Arteta’s £80m deal is simply indefensible
news.desc: The Premier League champions have told staff of plans to cut at least 60 jobs, writes Miguel Delaney , which completely goes against the club’s traditional values of ‘doing things the right way’
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
The Premier League champions have told staff of plans to cut at least 60 jobs, writes Miguel Delaney, which completely goes against the club’s traditional values of ‘doing things the right way’
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
The contrasts couldn’t be worse, and run right through Arsenal. Above all, though, there are the headline numbers.

A mere five days after Mikel Arteta signed one of the most lucrative managerial contracts in football, a £20m per year deal amid all manner of pageantry, the club staged a call to announce plans to cut 60 jobs - although there is the potential for this to come down.
People on everyday wages are now fearing for their jobs and mortgages, as the show just goes on.

Many staff members had feared this for some time, especially since the expensive consultancy firm Boston Consultancy Group [BCG] had been brought to examine the business earlier this year, but that seemed to jar with how – in the words of multiple sources – the football side has been “more and more indulged”.

The men’s and women’s performance departments, which represent well over half of the club's outgoings, isn’t to be touched in this round of redundancies. The manager has total control there, anyway, and did admittedly make considerable changes in the summer.
Arsenal had even planned for a blockbuster move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr in the summer, and one of the lines at the time was that the wages could be made up on image rights alone.
Now, the image of the club is sullied, as employees under threat of losing wages that would barely pay for two days of some Arsenal stars.
“You’re concentrating on the 10 per cent of the club, where most of the people are on everyday wages,” as one insider says.
This is always one of the most galling things when any major club plans such cuts, as was the case with Arsenal themselves back in 2020.
Or, as one source put it, you’d spend years trying to make up the money that went out on contracts for Fabio Vieira, Reiss Neilson and so many others.
“Players were on £100,000 a week to be crash test dummies in training”, a source said.
That might be football, sure, but the point is it doesn’t need to impinge on staff lives. That’s where it’s, once again, indefensible.
It’s even worse when the last accounts showed a club-record revenue of £691m. Arsenal are expected to reach £800m next.

The rationale behind this is said to be “cost efficiency” rather than “cost cutting” and to take the club to a next stage. And while 60 is the current number, that could come down, while it is possible that a lot of the roles could be redeployed.
As one insider says, however, “this wasn’t necessary and cuts more muscle than fat, potentially bringing more cost than benefit”. And it is still people losing jobs.
So much for success on the pitch translating into health off it, as has previously been seen at comparable models like Liverpool.
The celebratory mood from May’s long-awaited title is so quickly undercut by gloom about this.
That aspect is something that shouldn’t be overlooked in such stories, even if it should be secondary to concerns over people’s livelihoods.
Arteta talks about club “culture” probably more than any manager, and he has worked hard to build up that identity again, but these kinds of decisions directly corrode that.

Arsenal only have to ask counterparts at Manchester United. Those close to Sir Jim Ratcliffe say there was eventually some regret at the cuts they made, because it didn’t really achieve anything other than dismal headlines and a worse mood.
It affected the sense of unity that is actually crucial to sport, as well as the sense of community that these social institutions are supposed to stand for.
Most of them, under modern ownerships, often behave rather differently.
It is the crucial intangible that these kinds of hierarchies miss when striving for “efficiency”, as the BCG consultancy was intended to achieve.

And this is where the entire story is so integral to wider themes, from the Independent Football Regulator publishing a “State of the Game” review that is specifically intended to protect clubs’ community roles, to a debate about ownership that has been sharpened by the Manchester City crisis.
Much of this comes down to classic American corporatism, the ownership type that represents the other major force imposing itself on football in parallel to Gulf state wealth.
You can repeat all of the known lines about such leaderships only ever being interested in growth, when that is not what a football club exists for.

A football club – even the biggest in the world – only exist to play football for the local community they represent. They don’t actually need to do anything more to be sustainable, which a club with an immense global fanbase can obviously be. And that in a game awash with money due to that unique global popularity.

The business element is only something that has been bolted on over the past 30 years, as old rules on directors – that Friar lived through – were bypassed by stock market flotation and the rise of the Premier League.
Numerous insiders still say this is all even more acute with Kroenke Sports and Entertainment.
Stan Kroenke, the patriarch whose main background is real estate, has always been obsessed with margins.
Those on the American side of their sports empire state this has often been centred on numbers, and especially staff.
Moves like this are an inevitable consequence, and feel all the worse when they so jar with Arsenal’s self image of “doing things the right way”.
Other sources put it in the context of considerable change at executive level over the past year, which has created new pressures.
Kroenke likes low margins, and here are the margins being made lower, even if they are infinitesimal.
CEO Richard Garlick has been a corporate face of late, doing a series of media appearances and conferences to talk about how the club was transformed over the past half-decade.
Only last week, at Leaders at Stamford Bridge, he was talking about how this is only a beginning and the club now needed to show "confidence".
Well, what's this? This round of redundancies is something the old traditional Arsenal would not have considered.

news.title: Vinicius Jr to miss El Clasico against Barcelona after receiving four-game ban
news.desc: The Real Madrid winger will miss the games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander ⁠and Valencia after his red card on Saturday
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
The Real Madrid winger will miss the games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander ⁠and Valencia after his red card on Saturday
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Vinicius Jr will miss Real Madrid’s first Clasico of the season against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee handed the Brazil forward a four-match suspension on Wednesday.
The attacker was sent off for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba after coming off the bench during Saturday's 1-0 win over Villarreal.

The committee handed down a two-match ban for the red card and added a further two games for his protests to the referee, according to the disciplinary report from the eighth round of LaLiga fixtures.

The suspension rules Vinicius out of league matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia, leaving coach Jose Mourinho without one of his most heavily used forwards for the trip to Camp Nou.
Vinicius has started all but one of Real’s matches this season.
The winger was celebrating his second goal of the match against Villarreal when referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was summoned by the video assistant to examine the build-up to the strike.
The goal was ultimately disallowed after review showed Vinicius Jr pulling the hair of Saliba as they sprinted down the field.
A straight red card was then shown to Vinicius Jr, forcing Madrid to play with 10 men from the 73rd minute onwards.
The dismissal led to angry confrontations on the pitch as the forward shouted at Diaz de Mera while teammates attempted to restrain him.
Manager Jose Mourinho had initially joined the goal celebrations, but the decision left him incensed.
He subsequently missed the mandatory post-match press conference, reportedly out of concern that making comments about the refereeing would trigger a suspension.
The manager had already been shown a yellow card earlier in the fixture and was repeatedly restrained by backroom staff after prior decisions were made against his team.
Following the incident, he used social media to apologise to his teammates and Real Madrid fans.
The Clasico takes place on 25 October, with Real travelling to .eague leaders Barcelona

news.title: Fifa poised for rule change to avoid Folarin Balogun scandal repeat
news.desc: Folarin Balogun’s World Cup ban was suspended after Donald Trump revealed he called Gianni Infantino over the red card
text: Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in
Folarin Balogun’s World Cup ban was suspended after Donald Trump revealed he called Gianni Infantino over the red card
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Fifa is preparing to alter its regulations to prevent any repeat of the controversy surrounding Folarin Balogun.

A dispute over political interference erupted after Fifa’s disciplinary committee opted to suspend an automatic one-match ban handed to the United States forward during the World Cup. The intervention came after US president Donald Trump publicly disclosed that he had personally phoned Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino to request a review of the decision.
A proposal to explicitly prohibit the suspension of automatic one-game bans in the future is expected to be introduced at Thursday’s Fifa Council meeting in Zurich.

However, the regulatory change alone is unlikely to satisfy critics seeking a full explanation of how Balogun’s suspension was set aside. Among those seeking answers is Football Association chair and Fifa vice-president Debbie Hewitt, who wrote to Infantino last month requesting the disclosure of all documents related to the case.
Infantino has consistently maintained that the disciplinary panel reached its decision independently of his office.

Hewitt and fellow Council members are also expected to press Infantino for further details regarding the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. The initiative aimed to bring private investment into a commercial arm that would oversee the financial rights of the World Cup and other major tournaments.

The Swiss official faced calls to step down over the summer from the presidents of three continental confederations, including Uefa, after details of the FFE plan - developed without consulting the Fifa Council - were disclosed in media reports.

While Infantino appeared under severe pressure initially, he remains intent on standing for a fourth term as president at next year’s Fifa Congress and holds a strong position. Last week, he secured unanimous backing from the Confederation of African Football (CAF), alongside robust support across South America, Oceania, and Asia.

The president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa, who urged Infantino to resign in August, appeared to soften his stance last month in a letter advocating for an internal working group to explore governance reforms.
Uefa has committed to putting forward a credible opposition candidate before the 18 November deadline, but Infantino presents a formidable challenge for any contender.
The Fifa Peace Prize is also listed for discussion on Thursday following a request from a Council member.
Reports indicate the Council is seeking clarity on the process for this year's award, which was presented to President Trump for the first time last December.
Infantino may also face questioning regarding Fifa’s lease for office space in New York's Trump Tower, where the governing body reportedly agreed to pay $4 million (just over £3m) over seven years.
Additionally, reports surfaced this week that Infantino received a £1.3m payment in 2024 from an American Fifa World Cup subsidiary company that was omitted from Fifa’s annual financial report.

The Council is also set to consider a proposal from Fifa administrators to distribute $6.35 billion (£4.8bn) to member nations and continental confederations over the next three years, including $25 million (£19m) to each of Fifa’s 211 member countries.
That allocation would more than double the amount originally scheduled for distribution in the 2027 to 2030 cycle.

The plan follows a letter sent to Infantino on 18 September by the presidents of Uefa and Concacaf, urging that every national association receive an additional $10 million (£7.6m) through a single release from Fifa’s cash reserves, estimated at $6 billion (£4.5bn).

Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani stated that releasing the funds would demonstrate that member bodies "should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits".
The remarks were seen as a direct reference to FFE, as Fifa had previously pledged increased development funding to federations if the project was approved.
Fifa has been approached for comment on the proposed financial increase.
The Council is also expected to confirm host nations for several competitions, including the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup in 2028, with the US regarded as the front-runner to stage the event.
